article.articleHeadline: WHO Begins Trial for Ebola Outbreak | Biotech And Pharma
article.articleSummary: As of 1 August 2026, more than 3,500 people have been infected with Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD) in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, the second-largest Ebola outbreak on record, with no approved treatments or vaccines for BVD. The WHO launched enrollment for The PARTNERS trial to test MBP-134 (a monoclonal antibody from Mapp Biopharmaceutical funded by BARDA), remdesivir, or their combination to improve survival in laboratory-confirmed BVD patients. All MBP-134 doses are donated by BARDA/HHS, and Gilead Sciences is donating remdesivir for the study. The WHO Technical Advisory Group selected these therapies after reviewing preclinical and prior outbreak data. Enrolled patients of all ages receive close follow-up for at least 28 days. WHO Director-General Tedros Ghebreyesus noted that safe and effective therapeutics could save many lives in this outbreak.

Reports celebrate major steps: Ebopep, a therapeutic, shows promise in Ituri, and the ChAdOx1 BDBV vaccine is being launched at Oxford. Yet headlines warn that trials are early and real-world efficacy, safety, and access must be demonstrated; health-system weaknesses risk stalling progress. The saturation of the outbreak is quantified: about 1,521 deaths reported in the DRC, underscoring a deadly and ongoing crisis. Cross-border spillover is noted, with Uganda reporting 20 confirmed cases and two deaths imported from the DRC. The analysis emphasizes that vaccines and treatments must reach remote care centers to alter transmission, while stressing logistical, funding, and supply challenges that could undermine scientific advances against the Bundibugyo Ebola variant.

article.articleHeadline: "Here the fear is leaving in a white body bag": the story of an MSF field worker inside the Ebola treatment center in the DRC.
article.articleSummary: Ebola remains a major outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo, with official deaths surpassing 1,500 in under three months and nearly 3,000 confirmed infections, concentrated in Ituri province in the northeast, accounting for about 90% of confirmed cases and over 80% of national deaths. MSF field workers inside a treatment center in Ituri describe meticulous, slow-paced care to prevent transmission, since Ebola spreads through bodily fluids. The human toll is stark: entire families arrive infected—grandfather, daughters, granddaughters—after a grandmother unknowingly transmitted the virus; a pregnant woman in her second trimester dies from hemorrhage, followed by a dignified and safe burial. Fear marks every temperature check and admission, with many fearing entering or leaving the center in a white body bag. The piece emphasizes that saving lives requires precise, careful actions rather than speed, amid an ongoing Congo outbreak.

article.articleHeadline: Cholera in the DRC: 3,124 dead across sixteen provinces, four official tallies that do not match.
article.articleSummary: Four official cholera tallies in the DRC do not align. As of 31 July 2026, the WHO reports 106,401 cholera cases and 3,124 deaths since the start of the year, while the 30 June epidemiological update tallies 28,567 cases and 815 deaths to 31 May, a gap of 77,834 cases. Between the two documents, roughly 9,000 new cases per week are implied. The weekly government series generally runs about 1,000–1,600 suspected cases, suggesting 30–45k cases over 30 weeks, not 106k. The epidemic spans 16–21 provinces, with 56 health zones affected; Nord-Kivu and Sud-Kivu together account for about half of cases, Kinshasa is the epicenter with about 30% per bulletin, and Zongo (Sud-Ubangi) reported 270 suspected in a single week. Most counts are suspected; laboratories confirm only marginally. Data come from WHO, the Congolese WHO office, and MSF's cholera treatment unit in Pakadjuma.

article.articleHeadline: Zhuhai Deploys Mosquito-Borne Infectious Disease Prevention and Control Measures, with Daily Protective Guidelines for Citizens.
article.articleSummary: Zhuhai authorities unveiled strengthened prevention and control for Aedes-borne diseases, focusing on chikungunya fever and dengue fever, amid hot, rainy weather and heavy travel. At a July 31 municipal meeting chaired by Wu Zetong, officials urged strict implementation of the '1113' emergency-disposal protocol to rapidly detect cases, escalate responses, and cut transmission chains. The plan targets source reduction at hotspots—agricultural markets, tourist areas, construction sites, old communities, inner waterways, and vacant lots—alongside enhanced vector surveillance, sentinel medical monitoring, and coordinated actions with Hengqin and Macau. Public health education, adequate supplies, and streamlined, flattened emergency command were emphasized. Daily protective guidance for residents includes: remove standing water (weekly for water plants; wash containers), ensure ventilation and dryness, install and seal screens and nets, use approved anti-mosquito products, and observe safety when spraying indoors. Outdoors, wear light clothing and apply repellents.

article.articleHeadline: Follow-up on infant infections at a Guangzhou postpartum confinement center: date for lifting prevention and control measures extended to August 4.
article.articleSummary: Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV) infections have been detected among several infants at Hui Ci Hu Ai Maternity Center Luxe Yuexiu Branch in Guangzhou’s Yuexiu District. Initial mild symptoms (cough, runny nose) progressed in some cases, with affected babies receiving medical care after leaving the facility. Public health authorities conducted supervision, improving ventilation and disinfection, and the center paused admitting new infants during the revision period. On July 30, the center forecast lifting prevention measures after eight days with no new cases, but on July 31 authorities extended the tentative lifting date to August 4. Access now requires appointment only; entrants undergo temperature checks, wear masks, and must not touch infants, with visits limited to up to three people and conducted via window. The event coincides with the August 1 implementation of GB/T 33855-2026, the national standard for maternal-infant health service institutions, expanding regulatory scope and mandating comprehensive infection-control records and staffing practices.

article.articleHeadline: Severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome enters peak season, Qingdao residents—please keep this "Tick Protection Guide".
article.articleSummary: Severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS), caused by Dabie bandavirus, is entering peak season in Qingdao as summer heat and humidity boost tick activity. Transmission is mainly tick-bite–driven in hills, mountains, forests, grass and shrubland; possible human infection via contact with blood, body fluids, or excretions of patients or deceased cases for caregivers and healthcare workers. Incubation is typically 7–14 days. Early signs include fever (often >38°C), fatigue, nausea/vomiting, poor appetite, diarrhea, myalgia, headache, lymphadenopathy, and bleeding tendencies; labs commonly show thrombocytopenia and leukopenia. Residents near rural/forested areas, hikers, landscapers, and caretakers are at higher risk. Prevention centers on avoiding tick bites: wear long sleeves/pants, tuck clothes, use DEET repellents, perform thorough body/pet checks, wash clothes and shower after outdoors, and keep yards clear of vegetation. If bitten or febrile with thrombocytopenia, seek prompt medical evaluation and disclose exposure history; proper tick removal and infection control are advised.

article.articleHeadline: Parasite incubation periods can last for decades! Those who love raw and marinated seafood should beware.
article.articleSummary: Raw-marinated seafood presents health risks from viral and bacterial infections. The practice of marinating fresh seafood (shrimp, crabs, shellfish) in mixtures such as white wine, soy sauce, garlic, and chili, then consuming without thorough cooking, can expose consumers to pathogens. Even high-alcohol marinades do not reliably sterilize foods; ethanol at typical culinary strengths (around 50–75%) may not kill certain viruses like norovirus and hepatitis B virus. Potential bacterial threats include Vibrio parahaemolyticus, Vibrio vulnificus, and Salmonella, which can cause diarrhea, abdominal pain, bloating, vomiting, and nausea, with rare progression to bacteremia and life-threatening illness. The article highlights summer-season risks and cautions that marination cannot guarantee safety, though some processing may reduce risks. No outbreak data, laboratory confirmation, or case counts are provided, and no locations are specified.

article.articleHeadline: Data from the China CDC: Nearly half of respiratory tract infection diagnoses in children under five are related to indoor air pollution — Viruses and pollutants are attacking babies' respiratory tracts together — China Finance Times Net
article.articleSummary: China CDC data link indoor air pollution to nearly half of acute respiratory infections (ARTI) in children under five, with over 1 million China-wide ARTI deaths annually and more than 50% attributable to indoor pollutants; risk rises 2–3x. Children are more vulnerable due to higher breathing rate, lower standing height (0.8–1.2 m) in polluted zones, and immature immunity. Dominant indoor pathogens include influenza, RSV, rhinovirus, and Mycoplasma pneumoniae, with SARS-CoV-2 positivity at 16.3% among sentinel influenza-like illness cases; pollutants such as formaldehyde, benzene, dust mites, and dampness amplify susceptibility, creating a synergistic “1+1>2” effect. Guidance distinguishes air disinfection machines (消字号备案) from ordinary purifiers; zero-ozone certification is mandatory under GB/T 4706.45-2024. The Air Fortress P3 model holds 消字号备案 FB241031-51 (XG1), CMA/CNAS, and zero ozone, reporting 99.99% disinfection for H1N1 and EV71, formaldehyde CADR 420 m³/h, PM CADR 520 m³/h, 28 dB noise, and baby-grade certifications. Takeaways: indoor air quality drives pediatric ARTI; purifiers may be insufficient; choose certified, zero-ozone air disinfection devices for nursery rooms.

triage.headline_ja: 中国疾病予防管理センターのデータ：5歳未満児の呼吸器感染症診断の約半数が室内大気汚染に関連——ウイルスと汚染物質が乳幼児の呼吸器を共に攻撃——中国財経時報網

article.articleHeadline: Nationwide Study Tracks Hepatitis B Reactivation and Liver Dysfunction
article.articleSummary: HBV reactivation and liver dysfunction were investigated in Chinese patients with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) treated with infliximab, a TNF-α inhibitor. In a nationwide study across centers, patients with IBD undergoing infliximab were screened for hepatitis B before therapy and monitored with HBV DNA and liver-function tests during treatment. China’s intermediate HBV endemicity, with about 70 million chronic carriers, places many IBD patients at risk of HBV reactivation when immunosuppressed. Baseline serology distinguished active/chronic infection from prior exposure; concurrent immunosuppression and IBD activity were considered as risk modifiers. The investigation characterized HBV‑related liver injury, which can accompany viral replication and rise in liver enzymes, potentially progressing to jaundice or liver failure. Findings support universal HBV screening prior to biologic therapy and antiviral strategies: prophylaxis for HBsAg‑positive patients, and a case-by-case approach for resolved infection, guided by HBV DNA status and immunosuppression level. Emphasizes multidisciplinary HBV safety beyond gastroenterology.

triage.headline_ja: 全国調査：インフリキシマブ治療中のB型肝炎再活性化と肝機能障害を追跡
triage.triage_reason: 免疫抑制療法中のHBV再活性化に関する臨床研究であり、公衆衛生上の急性感染症アウトブレイクではないため、シグナルとしての該当性は低い。

article.articleHeadline: The Tiny Snails and Slugs That Can Turn Rat Lungworm into a Human Health Risk
article.articleSummary: Angiostrongylus cantonensis, rat lungworm, was described in 1933 in Guangzhou by H.T. Chen. Its life cycle requires rats as definitive hosts and snails or slugs as intermediate hosts; larvae migrate to the rat lungs, are shed in feces, infect gastropods, mature, then return to rats. Humans are incidental hosts via consumption of unwashed produce (notably lettuce) or paratenic hosts such as freshwater prawns, frogs, or fish. In humans, larvae enter the CNS and can cause eosinophilic meningitis; symptoms include neck pain, numbness, photophobia, headache, fever, and fatigue; severe cases can cause paralysis, coma, disability, or death. Since Guangzhou, A. cantonensis has spread across Southeast Asia, the Pacific Islands, Latin America, Australia, and warm parts of the U.S. (Hawaii, Florida, Gulf Coast) via ships, the pet trade (Achatina fulica, Pomacea), and climate change. Diagnosis relies on CSF eosinophils; prevention emphasizes washing produce and cooking potential hosts to 165°F.

triage.headline_ja: ヒトの健康リスクとなる広東住血線虫を媒介する小さなカタツムリとナメクジ
triage.triage_reason: 本記事は広東住血線虫（ラットラングワーム）の生物学・歴史・一般的拡散状況を解説する教育的記事であり、特定国での急性アウトブレイクや新規発生を報じるものではない。
triage.notes: 記事は1933年の広州での初記載や病原体の生活環、世界的分布の一般的解説であり、現在進行中の特定国でのアウトブレイクを報じるものではないため、対象国での実発生イベントとしては扱わない。

article.articleHeadline: COVID, in the never-revealed dossier, the true story of the virus in Italy | Libero Quotidiano.it
article.articleSummary: January 2020 marked the arrival of COVID-19 in Italy, but Libero Quotidiano’s ongoing dossier argues the country was ill-prepared. The series draws on documents and testimonies from the Parliament’s Covid commission. It cites a national pandemic plan last updated in 2006 and notes EU guidance to refresh it every three years, which Italy failed to do under ministers Beatrice Lorenzin (2013–2018) and Giulia Grillo (2018–2019) and later Roberto Speranza. Experts like Giuseppe Ippolito urged applying the plan’s method to a coronavirus threat. The report alleges masks were sent to China while Italian hospitals faced shortages, and a pre-lockdown meeting was not formally recorded. On January 13, ENAC signed a Memorandum with the People’s Republic of China to expand air links to 164 weekly flights (108 immediate). Paola De Micheli boasted of Europe’s highest China flight count. The series aims to illuminate responsibility and missed opportunities in the pandemic’s early phase.

triage.triage_reason: 本記事は2020年当時のイタリアのパンデミック対応の不備を検証する回顧的な調査報道であり、現在進行中の感染症発生シグナルではない。
triage.notes: 記事は2020年のCOVID-19パンデミック初期対応に関する過去の政治的責任追及の調査報道であり、現在の感染症発生事案ではない。中国への言及は航空便合意についてであり、疾病発生とは無関係。イタリアは対象国リストに含まれず、中国についても実際の疾病発生を報じる内容ではないため、verified_locationsは空とした。

article.articleHeadline: 9 pigs in Cebu City test positive for ASF
article.articleSummary: ASF detected in Cebu City, Philippines, with nine pigs in Barangay Quiot testing positive after three of 22 died, leaving 19 tested; nine were positive. All 19 pigs were culled with the raiser’s permission, as officials aim to contain local transmission. Dr. Jessica Maribujoc, head of DVMF, said contamination is local and that the raiser is the barangay’s only hog producer, located far from the general population in a mountainous area near the barangay border. Biosecurity measures urged include cleaning and weekly disinfection of trucks and pigpens, keeping feeds away, separating other animals, washing hands, bathing and changing clothes on arriving home, footwear outside the pen, and limiting visitors and gadgets near pigs. Officials also encouraged pig registration and insurance to enable government assistance if illness occurs.

article.articleHeadline: US, Philippines forge P42B partnership to combat HIV, tuberculosis
article.articleSummary: On 2026-08-01, the United States Embassy in the Philippines and the Department of Health signed a five-year, P42 billion Health Strategic Objective Agreement to enhance the Philippines’ capacity to detect, treat, and prevent HIV and tuberculosis (TB). Finalized on July 22, the partnership is a co-investment: the Philippines commits over P30 billion and the United States contributes more than P11.8 billion over the next five years. The goal is to bolster health systems and disease control for HIV and TB, including surveillance, diagnostics, treatment, and prevention. US Ambassador to the Philippines Lee Lipton described the signing as elevating bilateral cooperation. Location of the agreement is Manila, Philippines, with a five-year duration and a total funding mix of P42B (Philippines >P30B, US >P11.8B).

triage.headline_ja: 米国とフィリピン、HIV・結核対策のために420億ペソ規模のパートナーシップを締結

article.articleHeadline: Dengue cases in Cebu rising
article.articleSummary: Dengue in Cebu Province, Philippines, recorded 381 confirmed cases in July as rainfall spurs transmission. No outbreak is declared in Cebu City, but officials warn rising dengue during the rainy season and have activated dengue fast lanes in 16 Capitol-run provincial and district hospitals to speed assessment and treatment of suspected cases: immediate triage, quicker laboratory testing, closer monitoring, and early medical intervention. While PHO officials say the province has no outbreak, case numbers have grown over the past three months. Toledo City leads with 49 cases, followed by Barili (39), Talisay City (34), Consolacion (33); Carcar City and Medellin each with 19. Other areas include Cordova and Dalaguete (17), Sogod (14), Danao City (13), and Argao, Balamban, and Compostela (12 each).

triage.headline_ja: セブ州でデング熱患者が増加
triage.triage_reason: セブ州で雨季に伴うデング熱患者数の季節的増加が報告されているが、アウトブレイク宣言はなく、重症度や医療体制への負荷等の詳細情報が不足しているため、続報を注視する。

article.articleHeadline: DVMF: Cebu City ASF case likely caused by backyard pig movement
article.articleSummary: African Swine Fever (ASF) case in Cebu City, Philippines, with laboratory confirmation of nine ASF-positive pigs among 22 at the affected backyard farm; initial mayoral figure of 20 infected later corrected. In total, 19 pigs were culled after containment within four days. DVMF attributes spread to movement of pigs among backyard raisers and weak biosecurity; possible introduction via an owner-brought pig, and sharing of pork from a previously slaughtered pig with nearby residents; tracing points to purchases from Talisay City. Measures include intensified surveillance, 24-hour border control, and border monitoring; Barangay Quiot identified as affected, with information drives in Inayawan and Cogon Pardo; urging pig registration, livestock insurance, and strict biosecurity; swill feeding discouraged. Virus can survive long in the environment: months to years in blood, manure, and frozen pork. As of 1 Aug 2026, no additional lab-confirmed cases; outbreak controlled but not yet ASF-free.

article.articleHeadline: Smallpox deaths have doubled
article.articleSummary: Malappuram, Kerala: Smallpox cases surge in 2026 with 2280 cases reported up to July, including 1367 confirmed and 913 suspected; 61 deaths so far, of which 53 are suspected to be due to smallpox, yielding about a 5% case fatality. In July alone, 624 cases and 40 deaths were reported. The disease progresses rapidly, causing liver and kidney failure that can lead to death within days; key symptoms include fever, headache, severe fatigue, and muscle pain, with jaundice accompanying fever potentially indicating smallpox. Transmission is described as linked to water and soil contaminated with urine from animals such as foxes, jackals, cats, dogs, and cattle, with higher incidence among workers in rainy-season muddy or stagnant water. Health authorities urge prompt treatment and caution against delays. The article notes an ongoing outbreak in the state but provides no details on laboratory methods or imported/exported cases.

article.articleHeadline: Bangladesh records highest Dengue mortality rate globally
article.articleSummary: Bangladesh records the highest dengue mortality rate globally amid monsoon-driven spread. In 2026, 15,153 dengue infections with 53 deaths (13 in June, 35 in July) yield a 0.49% mortality rate, the highest in South Asia, according to WHO. Sri Lanka reports 76,000 cases with 57 deaths; India 0.08%, Sri Lanka 0.06%, Pakistan 0.05% mortality. The article links the rise to new dengue serotypes, lingering measles immunity amnesia, and persistent healthcare gaps. Outside Dhaka, mosquito larvae are more prevalent; Barisal Division sees 3,308 cases, with Dhaka Division at 38% of infections, yet deaths remain high in the capital. Entomologist Kabirul Bashar cites Breteau Index measurements indicating widespread larvae both inside and outside Dhaka; expert warnings that control campaigns are insufficient year-round. Officials acknowledge gaps between recommendations and action and call for community-engaged, year-round vector control, targeting Aedes breeding grounds.

article.articleHeadline: Why is Kerala facing high leptospirosis mortality?
article.articleSummary: Leptospirosis in Kerala, India, caused by pathogenic Leptospira, has been endemic since 1989 and now represents the state’s highest-mortality communicable disease. Cases surge with the Southwest monsoon; heavy rains, floods, and sustained humidity sustain bacteria in soil and water, exposing paddy workers, agricultural and construction laborers, and others handling contaminated water. Over the past three years Kerala records about 5,000 cases and nearly 400 deaths annually (confirmed and probable). In July this year the state reported ~50 deaths. Symptoms range from fever, myalgia, conjunctival suffusion and GI issues to rapid progression of pulmonary hemorrhage and multi-organ failure within 4.5–5 days. Late diagnosis and limited 24/7 emergency care heighten mortality; serology (ELISA) is often non-confirmatory in the acute phase, though PCR exists but is unevenly available. Doxycycline prophylaxis (200 mg twice weekly) targets high-risk groups, though compliance is poor. 2025 deaths: manual laborers 36.75%, agricultural 10.94%, homemakers gardening 10.16%.

triage.headline_ja: なぜケララ州はレプトスピラ症による高い死亡率に直面しているのか？
triage.triage_reason: ケララ州で1989年から常在するレプトスピラ症による高い死亡率が続いているが、異常・予想外な事象ではなく、ヒト-ヒト感染もなく国際的拡大リスクは低いため、フルRRAというより継続監視が妥当。
triage.notes: 本記事はインド・ケララ州における毎年恒例のモンスーン期に伴うレプトスピラ症流行の解説記事であり、1989年以来の常在疾患としての状況説明が中心。新規性・異常性は乏しく、感染経路は環境曝露（土壌・水を介した接触）であり人-人感染はない。

article.articleHeadline: Rain has driven up infections; hospitals are crowded with patients; contaminated water in several colonies is also a reason.
article.articleSummary: As of 1 August 2026, monsoon rains in Indore have driven a surge of infections: vomiting, diarrhoea, dehydration, plus viral illnesses, dengue and malaria. Hospitals report a sharp rise in kidney infections, with 40–50 patients daily at the Government Super Speciality Hospital. Many began with urinary tract infections, vomiting or diarrhoea and progressed due to delayed care or self-medication. Contaminated water is identified as the primary source, and several colonies still receive dirty supply. Residents of Scheme No. 54, Scheme No. 78, Gauri Nagar, Lasudia, Vijaynagar, Nagin Nagar, and Bhamori report persistent dirty water and ongoing complaints via 311/CM Helpline without timely remediation. People boil water or add substances to make it drinkable, underscoring a public health risk in Indore.

triage.headline_ja: 雨により感染症が増加、病院は患者で混雑；複数のコロニーの汚染水も原因
triage.triage_reason: 季節性のデング・マラリア・水系感染症の増加であり、地域的な公衆衛生問題だが国際的拡大や渡航制限の懸念は低い。ただし汚染水問題の継続と症例数増加は経過観察が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Dr G.P. Talwar: How India pioneered a new leprosy vaccine
article.articleSummary: Leprosy, caused by Mycobacterium leprae, remains linked to host immune response, especially in multibacillary forms. Indian immunologist Gursaran Pran Talwar developed an immunotherapeutic vaccine from a harmless, cultivable mycobacterium—initially designated Mycobacterium w and later named Mycobacterium indicus pranii (MIP)—to train the patient’s immune system. The approach complements, not replaces, multidrug therapy (MDT); heat-killed M. w is used alongside antibiotics to boost bacterial clearance and induce immune changes such as lepromin positivity. In multibacillary leprosy, vaccinated patients showed faster bacterial clearance and reductions in bacterial indices. A landmark study in the Journal of Infectious Diseases documented improved outcomes with combined MDT and M. w vaccination. Field trials extended to endemic regions, including Uttar Pradesh, involving thousands of household contacts and patients, with protective effects observed over several years. Talwar’s work reframed leprosy treatment as a three-way interaction among pathogen, medicine, and host immunity.

triage.headline_ja: G.P.タルワール博士：インドがハンセン病新ワクチンを開発した経緯

article.articleHeadline: Dengue-Chikungunya attack intensifies; 4 positives reported.
article.articleSummary: In Jabalpur, four dengue-positive cases were reported near IT Park: a man; a woman from Bedaghat; a woman from Dhanvantari Nagar; and a student from the Medical College Girls’ Hostel. Bedaghat and Dhanvantari Nagar residents also tested positive for chikungunya. January–July 2026 totals for Jabalpur district: dengue 29 cases, chikungunya 21 cases. Earlier cases included a 30-year-old man and a 48-year-old man with dengue near the Andhmook Bypass area, and three new chikungunya cases from the same vicinity (42-, 45-, and 56-year-old men) presenting with joint pain and fever. Authorities urge vigilance and prompt medical consultation for fever. Public health actions include larval control in public areas, intensified surveillance around Medical College Hospital Gadha and Dhanvantari Nagar, Dengue Dry Day with weekly fogging, house-to-house larva surveys, and larva clearance in hospital campuses and the Collectorate.

triage.headline_ja: デング熱・チクングニヤの感染拡大、4件の陽性反応が報告される
triage.triage_reason: インド・ジャバルプールでの季節性デング熱・チクングニヤの局地的発生であり、当局は通常の媒介蚊対策を実施中。重症例や死亡の報告はなく、国際的拡大の兆候もないが、蚊媒介感染症の継続的な発生状況として経過観察が妥当。
triage.notes: 毎年恒例のデング・チクングニヤの季節性流行と考えられ、地方当局によるフォギングや幼虫駆除等の通常対策が実施されている。地方紙（ヒンディー語）のみの報道で全国的・国際的な関心の高まりは確認できない。

article.articleHeadline: Two measles patients detected in Narkatiaganj; health department on alert; a special campaign launched in the village.
article.articleSummary: Measles detected in Gokhula village, Narkatiaganj block, West Champaran: two confirmed cases, a 13-year-old girl Divya Kumari and a 9-year-old boy Gulshan Kumar, with positive lab results after samples were sent to Patna. Following confirmation, health authorities activated surveillance, conducted a health survey of 204 children aged 9 months to 5 years, and distributed vitamin A. A special measles vaccination campaign has been launched to immunize eligible children; ANMs and other health workers instructed to report suspected cases promptly for testing and treatment. Medical teams are monitoring affected households to prevent spread. Measles is highly contagious and spreads via respiratory droplets; typical symptoms include high fever, dry cough, runny nose, red eyes, Koplik spots, and a spreading rash. Vaccination under the national program is emphasized.

article.articleHeadline: SMS awaits culture reports to find cataract infection source
article.articleSummary: Five patients with severe post-cataract infections at Kuchaman City's government's hospital were sampled for culture to identify the organism and trace the source. The surgeries occurred on July 28; all five were moved to Jaipur's SMS Hospital and underwent vitrectomy on July 30, with antibiotics started immediately. Culture results are awaited to confirm the causative organism and determine if the current antibiotic regimen should be changed. Findings may help investigators assess whether infections stemmed from surgical instruments, consumables, medicines, sterilisation lapses, or another common exposure at the facility. Outcomes depend on infection severity at treatment start, retinal involvement, and response to intensive medical and surgical management over the next days, with visual prognosis closely monitored.

article.articleSummary: COVID-19 cases are rising in Hanoi, with weekly infections nearly doubling to 185 across 76 communes and wards, up from 96 in 49 areas the previous week. 2026 confirmed COVID-19 cases total 588; fatalities remain at zero. Authorities also monitor dengue, hand, foot, and mouth disease, and whooping cough, anticipating seasonal increases. Preventive advice includes masking in crowded places and healthcare facilities, good hand hygiene, avoiding close contact with symptomatic individuals, and seeking prompt care for severe respiratory symptoms; older adults and those with underlying conditions should stay vigilant.

article.articleHeadline: Rainy season arrives; beware the risk of Japanese encephalitis in children.
article.articleSummary: Rainy season (May–September) in Vietnam drives Culex mosquitoes transmitting Japanese encephalitis virus, raising risk. Hanoi reported a 13-year-old with JE who had completed three vaccine doses but missed the booster, illustrating waning immunity. Vaccines do not confer lifelong protection; an immunity gap increases infection risk. JE virus cycles among mosquitoes, birds, and pigs; most infections are asymptomatic, but CNS invasion can cause fever, severe headache, vomiting, seizures, neck stiffness, altered consciousness, and coma, with mortality about 20–30% and substantial long-term neurological deficits among survivors. No specific antiviral exists; treatment is supportive. Vietnam vaccines include Imojev (two doses from 9 months to <18 years, one year apart; 18+: one dose) and Jevax (three-dose schedule from 12 months; second 1–2 weeks after first; third one year after; boosters every 3 years). Parents should track records, ensure full schedules, and combine vaccination with mosquito precautions and prompt medical care during illness.

article.articleHeadline: How do Hepatitis A, B, C, D, and E spread and affect the body?
article.articleSummary: Five hepatitis viruses—A, B, C, D, and E—are distinct pathogens that all damage the liver but differ in transmission, progression, and prevention. In Vietnam's public health guidance, misconceptions are addressed: A and E spread mainly via the fecal-oral route through contaminated food or water; A is typically acute with full recovery, while E is usually acute but can be severe in pregnancy, preexisting liver disease, or immunocompromise. B and C spread primarily through blood and body fluids; B can be transmitted mother-to-child, sexually, or via blood, and may become chronic, while C is mainly blood-borne and often chronic with risks of cirrhosis, liver failure, and cancer. D only infects people with B and worsens liver damage; preventing B also prevents D. Vaccines exist for A and B; C has no vaccine; E prevention relies on hygiene and safe water. Those at risk should seek evaluation.

article.articleHeadline: Australia backs fight against drug-resistant tuberculosis
article.articleSummary: Australia backs regional capacity-building to fight drug-resistant tuberculosis (DR-TB) in Southeast Asia. Four-day PeerLINC-led training in Makati City, Philippines, gathered delegates from Cambodia, Indonesia, Lao PDR, Malaysia, Timor-Leste, Vietnam, and the Philippines. Organized by PeerLINC Knowledge Hub with TB Alliance and Tropical Disease Foundation, and funded by AusAID, the program emphasizes peer-to-peer learning and adapting newer, shorter, patient-centered regimens (BPaLM/BPaL) to local health systems. Field visits to health facilities in Makati and Pasay allowed evaluation of facility accessibility, testing availability, and feasibility of implementing DR-TB care in the Philippines. The event concluded with country-specific action plans for the coming year covering diagnostics, clinical care, patient support, and program management. Australia frames this as development cooperation that builds regional networks to address cross-border health challenges.

article.articleHeadline: Warning: Melioidosis is easily contracted during the rainy season.
article.articleSummary: Melioidosis (Whitmore), caused by Burkholderia pseudomallei, is a dangerous bacterial infection endemic to soil, mud, and contaminated water in tropical regions such as Vietnam. Transmission is environmental rather than person-to-person, increasing during the rainy season when the bacterium thrives in wet soil and water. The disease presents variably and can mimic pneumonia or other infections, potentially progressing to septicemia and multi-organ failure if untreated. In Phu Tho Province General Hospital, a 60-year-old man presented with swelling and pain near the right ear. A parotid gland abscess was drained; culture identified Burkholderia pseudomallei, initiating targeted antibiotics. The patient recovered. Another case in Quang Ninh involved a 43-year-old woman with septic shock and multi-organ dysfunction, rescued with VA-ECMO. Preventive measures include protective clothing, wound care, hand hygiene, drinking clean water, and managing chronic diseases; there is no vaccine yet.

article.articleHeadline: Tainan City reports one new imported dengue fever case | LIFE Lifestyle Network
article.articleSummary: One new imported dengue fever case was reported in Tainan City on July 30: a Taiwanese woman in Yongkang District (Liuhe Li) who traveled to Vietnam from June 23–29 and returned July 29. She developed fever July 28; after arrival at Kaohsiung Airport, an NS1 test was negative, but hospital PCR on July 30 confirmed dengue infection, the fifth imported case in Tainan. The Dengue Prevention Center promptly deployed fogging, environmental cleanup, vector density surveys, and health education to prevent spread. Nationally, Taiwan has 108 dengue cases as of July 31: 7 locally transmitted and 101 imported, with Indonesia the most common source, followed by Vietnam and the Maldives. Travelers are advised to use protective measures and seek care if fever develops after travel, noting travel history to physicians. Ongoing surveillance shows over 500,000 Aedes eggs collected; 56,175 households inspected; 6,822 standing-water containers found; 120 positive; 31,430 people educated.

article.articleHeadline: Undercover for several days, 35 tons of pigs contaminated with banned substances bound for Ho Chi Minh City were intercepted.
article.articleSummary: 35 tons of pigs contaminated with banned substances bound for Ho Chi Minh City were intercepted after covert overnight surveillance. Three lots, totaling 280 animals, tested positive for Beta-agonists—Salbutamol and Clenbuterol—with one lot also infected by African swine fever virus. All animals were culled. The shipments were destined for a Ho Chi Minh City slaughterhouse, highlighting risks of disease spread and food-safety violations during transport. Authorities emphasized the complex supply chains and the need for strict checks at city gates. In the first half of 2026, inspections of more than 14,000 food-producing facilities led to numerous violations and fines exceeding 11 billion VND, with 26 cases prosecuted for counterfeit or unsafe foods. The “Tick Green Responsibility” program expands to markets, schools, hospitals, industrial zones, and e-commerce to improve traceability. A separate incident involved nearly 200 ducks from Dong Nai to Ho Chi Minh City without a veterinary certificate.

The DI Yogyakarta BPKP team commits to ongoing, high-quality oversight for more effective, accountable public health outcomes.

article.articleHeadline: Don't Underestimate These Four Infectious Diseases That Could Lurk While You Swim in a Public Pool
article.articleSummary: Public swimming pools can transmit infections when sanitation and disinfection are not regularly maintained. Even swallowing a small amount of contaminated pool water can introduce pathogens, putting vulnerable groups—children, pregnant women, and the elderly—at risk of dehydration and skin rashes. The article highlights diarrhea and Legionnaires’ disease as waterborne risks. Pathogens implicated in pool-related diarrhea include Cryptosporidium, Giardia, Shigella, norovirus, and pathogenic E. coli, with Cryptosporidium being the most common and able to persist for days despite chlorine. Public pools typically require pre-swim showers to reduce transmission. Avoid entering pools if recently ill, and steer clear of unmonitored lakes or rivers where animals can spread contaminants. Diarrhea from pool water can last up to two weeks and may lead to severe dehydration; seek medical care promptly if symptoms occur.

article.articleHeadline: There are no new measles cases, but the Cirebon City Health Office cannot yet lift the outbreak status.
article.articleSummary: Measles outbreak status persists in Cirebon City, Indonesia, despite no new cases reported in 10 days. Lifting the KLB requires epidemiological criteria: at least 28 consecutive days without new cases (two incubation periods) and any new cases must not be epidemiologically linked to previous ones. Current evaluation still shows two linked cases from transmission among siblings, preventing cancellation of the outbreak status. Decision made via cross-sector review with camat, lurah, hospitals, Education Department, Religion Ministry, and Bappeda. Immunization coverage as of June 2026 is 34%, well below the first-half target of 47.5%, and far from the 95% threshold needed for herd immunity to halt transmission and protect infants not yet eligible for vaccination. The KLB has been in place since February 20, 2026 and will remain until criteria are met.

article.articleHeadline: Shanghai man in Thailand contracts brain-eating worm after eating raw salted seafood; severe intestinal ulcers with bleeding and shock, nearly dies.
article.articleSummary: Shanghai man Xu contracted Entamoeba histolytica amoebic dysentery in Thailand after consuming raw salted seafood, leading to massive intestinal ulcers, recurrent heavy bleeding, and septic shock upon his return to China. He underwent multiple surgeries as his condition deteriorated, with hemoglobin dropping below 6 g/dL, and spent more than 30 days receiving continuous, personalized care at Shanghai Public Health Clinical Center, ultimately stabilizing and surviving. Entamoeba histolytica, common in tropical/subtropical regions, can cause fulminant amoebic colitis with extensive bowel necrosis, bleeding, perforation risk, and may disseminate to the liver causing abscess. Mild cases are often misdiagnosed as gastroenteritis, delaying therapy. Travelers are urged to maintain strict food and water hygiene in tropical areas and seek urgent medical care for abdominal pain, diarrhea, or vomiting to avoid delays; this represents an imported case in Shanghai from Thailand.

article.articleHeadline: Parotid abscess, unexpectedly discovered infection with flesh-eating bacteria.
article.articleSummary: 60-year-old man in Phú Thọ, Vietnam, presented with swelling and pain near the right ear, initially diagnosed on 1 August as cellulitis with an abscess of the parotid gland. An incision and drainage was performed; pus sent for culture identified Burkholderia pseudomallei, the agent of Whitmore/Melioidosis. The infection is soil- and waterborne and can cause septicemia and multi-organ damage; the exposure timing remains unclear for this patient. He received antibiotics; fever resolved and the parotid abscess decreased. Melioidosis mortality can be high: septicemia-related deaths around 40–50% in Thailand/Singapore, and up to 75% with pneumonia. There is currently no vaccine. Protective measures include PPE for outdoor work, hand hygiene, and avoiding undercooked meat. Clinicians should consider melioidosis in persistent swelling with fever or pus and seek early hospital evaluation. Published 2 August 2026.

article.articleHeadline: Mexico will know in November whether it loses its measles-free status.
article.articleSummary: Mexico and the United States will face an independent epidemiological review in November to determine if they retain measles-free status, according to Pan American Health Organization (PAHO) Director Jarbas Barbosa. The commission will analyze epidemiologic data and issue a recommendation to the director. Barbosa noted that even if either country loses the status, it can be restored through vaccination, vigilant surveillance, and outbreak control—citing Brazil and Venezuela, which lost measles-free status in 2018 and later recovered. He stressed measles' high transmissibility and that outbreaks have caused deaths among indigenous and other vulnerable communities, and that elimination requires vaccination coverage above 95 percent, uniformly across all communities, not just national averages. International travel keeps reintroduction risk. The Americas had achieved measles freedom but Canada’s criteria lapse ended that status. Barbosa also mentioned future pandemic preparedness and a One Health approach, plus Argentina and Brazil's leading mRNA vaccine projects.

Campaign windows run Aug 1–6 (Blue Nile, Red Sea, North Kordofan, Nile), Aug 2–7 (Kassala), and Aug 10–15 (Khartoum, Northern State). The diphtheria vaccine is safe, free, and effective after three doses; families should bring vaccination cards for verification. A federal coordination chamber will monitor readiness.

article.articleHeadline: National campaign warns about the risks of RSV and reinforces the importance of vaccination for pregnant women and infants.
article.articleSummary: RSV (Respiratory Syncytial Virus) presents a major risk to Brazilian children under two, driving bronchiolitis and pneumonia with severe outcomes and deaths concentrated in this age group. Brazil’s Sociedade Brasileira de Imunizações launched the campaign “Todos contra o VSR - Proteção desde o Início” to educate pregnant women, the general public, and health professionals. Two protective strategies are emphasized: (1) maternal vaccination against RSV starting at 28 weeks of gestation to transfer antibodies to the fetus, protecting newborns; and (2) monoclonal antibody prophylaxis given to newborns, especially preterm infants and those with risk factors, as recommended by the Unified Health System (SUS). The awareness effort includes medical video lectures, a themed website, social media content, and video testimonials from mothers and clinicians, including Dr. Drauzio Varella, with support from multiple health institutions to underscore vaccination during pregnancy and newborn care as the most effective prevention of severe respiratory disease.

article.articleHeadline: Ministry of Health records first dengue death in 2026.
article.articleSummary: First dengue death in Mato Grosso do Sul in 2026: an 11-year-old boy from Bonito developed symptoms on June 20 and died eight days later; cause confirmed by the State Health Secretariat in the latest epidemiological bulletin. Two suspected dengue deaths are under investigation. The state reports 4,760 probable dengue cases this year, with 1,828 laboratory confirmations. Vaccination coverage remains low at 44.34% of the target, far from the 90% national goal; Novo Horizonte do Sul, Rio Negro, Angélica, and Figueirão reached or surpassed the target, while Campo Grande stands at 26.14%. Chikungunya cases rise to 12,735 probable, with 9,729 laboratory confirmations. Since January, chikungunya has caused 28 deaths in Mato Grosso do Sul, in Dourados, Bonito, Jardim, Fátima do Sul, Douradina, Guia Lopes da Laguna, Itaporã, Ponta Porã and Nioaque.

article.articleHeadline: Várzea Grande Zoonoses issues warning about rising positive cases and asks the public to pay attention to the signs of the disease.
article.articleSummary: Canine visceral leishmaniasis (LVC) is a rising concern in Várzea Grande, Brazil, an area long considered endemic, with increasing cases tied to expansion in neighborhoods like Jardim Maringá. LVC is a zoonosis caused by Leishmania sp., transmitted by sandflies (Lutzomyia longipalpis and related species); dogs are the main urban reservoir, elevating human risk. From January to June this year, the CCZ VG recorded nearly 500 tests on dogs suspected of LVC, signaling rising transmission. Classic canine symptoms include progressive weight loss with normal appetite, liver and spleen involvement, skin ulcers, and non-healing wounds, especially on the nose and ears. Euthanasia is only performed after confirmed diagnosis; Lacen provides final confirmation, with differential diagnoses including bacterial, fungal, autoimmune diseases, or mange. No mass vaccination; control emphasizes vector management and environmental measures, such as deltamethrin collars and yard cleaning. For testing, contact CCZ VG at Rua 42, Jardim Paiaguás I, (65) 98476-5719.

article.articleHeadline: Mato Grosso do Sul records more than 10,000 cases of viral hepatitis.
article.articleSummary: Mato Grosso do Sul, Brazil, registered 10,199 viral hepatitis cases and 986 deaths from 2000–2024, highlighting that early diagnosis boosts cure chances as infections can be silent and progress to cirrhosis, liver cancer, or transplant. Nationally, Brazil reported over 826,000 hepatitis cases (2000–2024): hepatitis C 342,328 (41.5%), hepatitis B 302,351 (36.6%), hepatitis A 174,977 (21.2%), with hepatitis D and E together <1%. In MS, hepatitis A accounted for the highest notifications during 2000–2024. To improve detection, the Health Ministry distributed rapid tests, with 60,000 hepatitis C tests delivered to MS by May 2026. Transmission differs by type: HAV via contaminated water/food; HBV/HDV via blood, unprotected sex, and mother-to-child; HCV via blood contact and non-sterile procedures. The Global Hepatitis Report 2026 cites ~1.3 million deaths in 2024 from HBV/HCV worldwide, challenging elimination by 2030.

article.articleHeadline: Leprosy, alarm grows in Florida: why an ancient disease is returning to the spotlight.
article.articleSummary: Leprosy (Hansen's disease) cases are rising in Florida but not an emergency, with 2025: 36 cases (27 locally acquired); by July 2026, 17 new cases, mostly in central Florida along I-4 and Brevard County. Transmission via Mycobacterium leprae occurs mainly through prolonged contact with an untreated person and respiratory secretions; casual contact is unlikely. The nine-banded armadillo is a known natural reservoir, but many recent patients report no armadillo contact or travel to endemic countries, prompting UF and the National Hansen's Disease Program to investigate environmental exposure and soil. Worldwide, WHO reports >170,000 new cases in 2024, with about 80% in India, Brazil, Indonesia; Europe reports imported cases. MDT introduced in the 1980s cures most if diagnosed early. Stigma and late diagnosis remain challenges; early treatment renders patients non-contagious; the true emergency is disability from late diagnosis.

article.articleHeadline: Dirty water, mud and debris increase the risk of disease after storms in the capital.
article.articleSummary: Storms in Campo Grande leave mud, debris, and sewage after flooding, raising disease risk and demanding careful cleanup. Avoid direct contact with contaminated areas, eliminate standing water, and seek medical care if fever, body aches, or malaise appear. Post-rain conditions favor Aedes mosquitoes, increasing dengue, Zika, and chikungunya risk. Floodwaters also bring waste and sewage into homes, enabling exposure to contaminated food and diseases such as leptospirosis, cholera, hepatitis, and typhoid fever. During cleanup, wear boots, gloves, and long sleeves; inspect footwear, clothing, and dark corners before handling; remove debris and food remnants to deter rats and insects. Keep water and food sealed and discard items damaged by floods. After rains, snakes, scorpions, spiders, and rodents may enter residences; do not capture or kill them—leave the area and contact authorities. For minor wounds, wash with soap and water and monitor for infection; seek care if fever or severe symptoms occur.

article.articleHeadline: Africa in July: Uganda's Ebola 'victory', strained S'Africa continental ties, Nigeria-Morocco gas pipeline
article.articleSummary: Uganda discharged the last Ebola patient in July, signaling a potential end to the outbreak and raising prospects of an Ebola-free status. In South Africa, xenophobic violence intensified, straining continental ties as Nigeria reported further fatalities: a Nigerian citizen, Ibeh Simon, and another were killed during a Cape Town SAPS operation, bringing current-wave Nigerian deaths to five and total killings since 2022 to about 98 (mob violence, hate crimes, and extrajudicial killings). A South African delegation to Abuja, led by Ronald Lamola, saw a downgraded meeting with President Tinubu. Ghana lodged a protest over a planned Ramaphosa visit, urging deferral until xenophobia issues are resolved, though officials stated the relationship remains intact. Ghana also moved to extend the presidential term from four to five years, extending Parliament similarly, lowering the presidential candidate age to 35, and shifting elections to the first week of November with a January inauguration timeline.
